questions.prompt: What is the most important step before formatting a disk?
options: A. Delete the files and look for a backup later
B. Get approval and verify a backup
C. Choose a random partition
D. Disable the user account
questions.answer: B. Get approval and verify a backup
questions.explanation:
B. Get approval and verify a backup

Formatting can erase data, so approval and a working backup must come first.

questions.prompt: What should you do when choosing a partition in Windows Setup?
options: A. Delete the first partition without checking
B. Confirm the correct disk and partition
C. Format every disk
D. Change partitions just to test
questions.answer: B. Confirm the correct disk and partition
questions.explanation:
B. Confirm the correct disk and partition

Choosing the wrong disk or partition can destroy unrelated files.

options: A. Try every setting
B. Understand and authorize the change, then record the old value
C. Always disable Secure Boot
D. Power off during an update
questions.answer: B. Understand and authorize the change, then record the old value
questions.explanation:
B. Understand and authorize the change, then record the old value

Make only understood, authorized changes and keep the original value so you can recover.

questions.prompt: Before reinstalling macOS, what should you do?
options: A. Verify a backup and follow official steps for the Mac model
B. Erase the disk immediately
C. Download an unknown installer
D. Put the Apple ID password in a support ticket
questions.answer: A. Verify a backup and follow official steps for the Mac model
questions.explanation:
A. Verify a backup and follow official steps for the Mac model

A verified backup and the correct official recovery steps reduce data-loss and setup risks.

questions.prompt: What can “erase disk” mean in a Linux installer?
options: A. Remove only temporary files
B. Delete data on the selected disk
C. Clear only the display
D. Make no changes
questions.answer: B. Delete data on the selected disk
questions.explanation:
B. Delete data on the selected disk

Erasing can remove data from the selected disk; stop and confirm before proceeding.
